metadata.title: Account Closure Procedure

text:
Account Closure Procedure

Procedure ID: MS-PRO-012 | Version 1.4 | Effective: June 1, 2026 | Owner: Member Services | Classification: Internal

1. Purpose

This procedure explains how Member Service Representatives (MSRs) and Member Contact Centre agents close Retail share and checking accounts at a member's request, and how remaining funds are returned. It does not cover closures initiated by Harbor for risk or policy reasons, which follow the Involuntary Closure Standard.

metadata.section_path: Account Closure Procedure > 2. Before You Begin
metadata.title: Account Closure Procedure

text:
Account Closure Procedure
2. Before You Begin

Confirm that the request comes from an owner of the account. For joint accounts, every owner must consent to the closure. Review the account for linked services that will fail once the account is closed, including direct deposits, automatic loan payments, bill pay payees, and person-to-person payment enrollments, and explain to the member which services they need to redirect.

Closing the Primary Share Account ends the member's membership. If the member has an open loan, the Primary Share Account cannot be closed until the loan is paid in full.

metadata.section_path: Account Closure Procedure > 3. Closure Steps
metadata.title: Account Closure Procedure

text:
Account Closure Procedure
3. Closure Steps

Step | Action | Owner
1 | Verify the member's identity using two forms of identification in branch or the three-factor authentication script by phone. | MSR or agent
2 | Obtain a signed Form HCU-ACL-220 (Account Closure Request) from every owner on the account. | MSR
3 | Review pending items, holds and scheduled transfers in the core system and note them on the form. | MSR
4 | Cancel debit cards, stop recurring transfers and remove bill pay payees linked to the account. | MSR
5 | Move the account to Closing status and record the requested disbursement method. | MSR
6 | Complete the pending items review described in Section 4. | Deposit Operations
7 | Disburse the remaining balance as described in Section 5 and set the account to Closed. | Deposit Operations
8 | Send the closure confirmation letter and retain the form in the member file. | Deposit Operations

Phone requests may be accepted for single-owner accounts only, and the signed form must be returned by mail or secure upload before step 5 can be completed.

metadata.section_path: Account Closure Procedure > 4. Pending Items Review
metadata.title: Account Closure Procedure

text:
Account Closure Procedure
4. Pending Items Review

Accounts with outstanding checks, pending ACH debits or unresolved card disputes are placed in Closing status for a 30-day review period before final disbursement. During the review period, deposits are rejected and items presented for payment are paid only up to the remaining balance. Accounts with no pending items may be disbursed on the next business day.

metadata.section_path: Account Closure Procedure > 5. Disbursement of Remaining Funds
metadata.title: Account Closure Procedure

text:
Account Closure Procedure
5. Disbursement of Remaining Funds

After the review period, the remaining balance is disbursed by official check mailed within 7 business days to the address on file. At the member's request, funds may instead be transferred to another Harbor member's account with that member's consent, or paid out in cash in branch if the balance is under $2,500. Dividends are paid through the date of closure.

If the account is overdrawn at closure, do not complete the closure. Refer the member to the Overdraft Policy and create a recovery case.

metadata.section_path: Account Closure Procedure > 6. Worked Example
metadata.title: Account Closure Procedure

text:
Account Closure Procedure
6. Worked Example

Example for training purposes: member [REDACTED-NAME] (member number [REDACTED-MEMBER]) called on 06/14/2026 to close Basic Checking account [REDACTED-ACCOUNT]. The agent verified identity, noted one outstanding check for $182.40, and mailed Form HCU-ACL-220 to [REDACTED-ADDRESS]. The signed form was returned on 06/19/2026. The check cleared on 06/22/2026, the review period ended, and a closing check for $1,006.18 was mailed on 07/21/2026.

metadata.section_path: Account Closure Procedure > 7. Records
metadata.title: Account Closure Procedure

text:
Account Closure Procedure
7. Records

Form HCU-ACL-220 and the closure confirmation letter are retained for five years after closure. Closed accounts are reported to the account screening agency only where the account was closed with a negative balance.

metadata.section_path: Business Account Fee Guide
metadata.title: Business Account Fee Guide

text:
Business Account Fee Guide

_Effective date: January 1, 2026 | Applies to: Business Services members | Owner: Business Services_

This guide lists the fees and limits that apply to Harbor Credit Union business deposit accounts. Consumer (Retail) accounts are governed by the Retail Schedule of Fees and Charges, the Overdraft Policy and the Wire Transfer Policy, which contain different amounts.

metadata.section_path: Business Account Fee Guide > Business Checking Products
metadata.title: Business Account Fee Guide

text:
Business Account Fee Guide
Business Checking Products

Business Essentials Checking has a monthly maintenance fee of $10.00, waived with an average daily balance of $2,500 or more. It includes 200 free transactions per statement cycle, after which each debit or deposited item is charged $0.40.

Business Analysis Checking is designed for higher-volume businesses. Balances in Business Analysis Checking earn an Earnings Credit Rate (ECR) of 0.35%, which offsets monthly service charges. Service charges not covered by the earnings credit are debited from the account after the end of each month. The monthly account maintenance fee is $15.00.

metadata.section_path: Business Account Fee Guide > Business Overdraft
metadata.title: Business Account Fee Guide

text:
Business Account Fee Guide
Business Overdraft

Business overdraft items are charged $35.00 each, up to five (5) per business day. Business accounts are not eligible for Courtesy Pay; overdrafts are paid only under an approved Business Overdraft Line of Credit or at Harbor's discretion. Transfers from a linked business savings account to cover an overdraft are charged $12.00 per transfer.

metadata.section_path: Business Account Fee Guide > Business Wire Transfers
metadata.title: Business Account Fee Guide

text:
Business Account Fee Guide
Business Wire Transfers

Outgoing domestic wires from Business accounts are charged $20.00 per wire. Outgoing international wires from Business accounts are charged $40.00 per wire. Incoming wires to Business accounts are charged $10.00 per wire. The same-day cutoff for business domestic wires submitted through Business Online is 4:00 p.m. Eastern Time. Business wires above $100,000 require dual approval by two authorized signers.

metadata.section_path: Business Account Fee Guide > Business Remote and Mobile Deposit
metadata.title: Business Account Fee Guide

text:
Business Account Fee Guide
Business Remote and Mobile Deposit

The standard Business mobile deposit limit is $25,000 per business day and $100,000 per rolling 30 days. Remote deposit capture with a desktop scanner is available for a monthly fee of $30.00 and carries limits set during underwriting.

metadata.section_path: Business Account Fee Guide > Business Debit Cards
metadata.title: Business Account Fee Guide

text:
Business Account Fee Guide
Business Debit Cards

Business debit cards have a daily ATM withdrawal limit of $1,000 and a daily purchase limit of $7,500. Higher limits may be approved by Business Services for established accounts.

metadata.section_path: Business Account Fee Guide > Other Business Services
metadata.title: Business Account Fee Guide

text:
Business Account Fee Guide
Other Business Services

- Stop payment order: $35.00 per request.

- Cash handling (currency deposited over $10,000 per month): $0.15 per $100.

- Night depository bags: $25.00 per bag set.

- ACH origination: $25.00 per month plus $0.10 per entry.

- Positive Pay: $40.00 per month.

Fees are subject to change with 30 days' written notice. Business members should contact their Business Relationship Manager with questions about pricing or earnings credit calculations.

metadata.section_path: Contact Centre Script: Lost or Stolen Card
metadata.title: Contact Centre Script: Lost or Stolen Card

text:
Contact Centre Script: Lost or Stolen Card

_Script ID: CC-SCR-007 | Version 2.2 | Last reviewed: March 3, 2026 | Owner: Member Contact Centre | Classification: Internal_

When to Use This Script

Use this script when a member reports that a Harbor debit or credit card has been lost, stolen, or retained by an ATM, or that they believe someone else knows the card number. Do not use it for disputes about a merchant charge; use the Card Dispute Procedure instead.

metadata.section_path: Contact Centre Script: Lost or Stolen Card > Step 1: Greeting and Authentication
metadata.title: Contact Centre Script: Lost or Stolen Card

text:
Contact Centre Script: Lost or Stolen Card
Step 1: Greeting and Authentication

AGENT: "Thank you for calling Harbor Credit Union, this is [AGENT FIRST NAME]. I understand your card may be lost or stolen. I'm going to help you secure it right away. First, I need to verify your identity."

[Complete the three-factor authentication script. If the caller cannot be authenticated, you may still block the card but must not discuss balances or transactions.]

metadata.section_path: Contact Centre Script: Lost or Stolen Card > Step 2: Block the Card
metadata.title: Contact Centre Script: Lost or Stolen Card

text:
Contact Centre Script: Lost or Stolen Card
Step 2: Block the Card

Place an immediate block on the card in CardCenter using status code 41 (lost) or 43 (stolen). Confirm the last four digits of the card with the member before applying the block.

AGENT: "I have blocked the card ending in [LAST FOUR]. It can no longer be used for purchases or ATM withdrawals."

metadata.section_path: Contact Centre Script: Lost or Stolen Card > Step 3: Review Recent Activity
metadata.title: Contact Centre Script: Lost or Stolen Card

text:
Contact Centre Script: Lost or Stolen Card
Step 3: Review Recent Activity

AGENT: "Let's look at the recent transactions together. Please tell me if there are any you don't recognize."

[Read transactions from the last 10 days. If the member identifies any unauthorized transactions, note them and proceed to Step 4. If none, skip to Step 5.]

metadata.section_path: Contact Centre Script: Lost or Stolen Card > Step 4: Fraud Referral
metadata.title: Contact Centre Script: Lost or Stolen Card

text:
Contact Centre Script: Lost or Stolen Card
Step 4: Fraud Referral

If the member reports unauthorized transactions, transfer the call to the Fraud Response Team at extension 4417 after completing Step 5. Use a warm transfer and summarize the case for the Fraud Response analyst before connecting the member.

metadata.section_path: Contact Centre Script: Lost or Stolen Card > Step 5: Compliance Disclosure (read aloud, verbatim)
metadata.title: Contact Centre Script: Lost or Stolen Card

text:
Contact Centre Script: Lost or Stolen Card
Step 5: Compliance Disclosure (read aloud, verbatim)

AGENT: "Please listen carefully to the following information. Because you have reported your card lost or stolen, you will not be responsible for unauthorized transactions made after this call. For unauthorized debit card transactions made before this call, your liability may depend on how quickly you reported the loss, as explained in your Electronic Fund Transfer Agreement and Disclosure. Harbor will investigate any transactions you dispute and will contact you in writing with the results. Do you understand this information?"

[Wait for a verbal "yes". If the member says no, read the disclosure again. Record the acknowledgment in the call notes.]

metadata.section_path: Contact Centre Script: Lost or Stolen Card > Step 6: Replacement Card
metadata.title: Contact Centre Script: Lost or Stolen Card

text:
Contact Centre Script: Lost or Stolen Card
Step 6: Replacement Card

Order a replacement card to the address on file. Do not change the mailing address on this call; address changes require separate verification.

AGENT: "I've ordered your new card. By standard mail, a replacement card typically arrives within 7 to 10 business days. You can add the new card to your mobile wallet as soon as it is activated. If you need it sooner, expedited delivery is available for a fee listed in our Schedule of Fees."

metadata.section_path: Contact Centre Script: Lost or Stolen Card > Step 7: Close the Call
metadata.title: Contact Centre Script: Lost or Stolen Card

text:
Contact Centre Script: Lost or Stolen Card
Step 7: Close the Call

AGENT: "Is there anything else I can help you with today? Thank you for calling Harbor Credit Union."

[Wrap-up code: CARD-LS. Call notes must include the block status code, the disclosure acknowledgment, whether a fraud referral was made, and the replacement delivery method.]

metadata.section_path: Card Dispute Procedure
metadata.title: Card Dispute Procedure

text:
Card Dispute Procedure

Procedure ID: CS-PRO-031 | Revision 5 | Effective: April 15, 2026 | Owner: Card Services | Classification: Internal

1. Purpose

This procedure sets out how Member Contact Centre agents and Card Services analysts receive, classify, investigate and resolve disputes on Harbor debit and credit cards. It is designed to meet the error-resolution requirements of Regulation E for debit cards and Regulation Z for credit cards, and the chargeback rules of the card network.

metadata.section_path: Card Dispute Procedure > 2. Intake and Timeframes
metadata.title: Card Dispute Procedure

text:
Card Dispute Procedure
2. Intake and Timeframes

Members must report an unauthorized or disputed card transaction within 60 days of the statement date on which the transaction first appeared. Disputes received after this period are still logged, but Harbor's liability protections and the member's right to provisional credit may be limited.

For every dispute, the agent completes Form HCU-DSP-114 (Card Transaction Dispute) during the initial contact, whether the contact is by phone, in branch, or through secure message. The form captures the transaction date, amount, merchant descriptor, the member's explanation, and whether the card is still in the member's possession.

1. Verify the caller using the standard three-factor authentication script.

2. Confirm the transaction details against the card processing system.

3. If fraud is suspected, block the card immediately and order a replacement.

4. Complete Form HCU-DSP-114 and read the dispute acknowledgment disclosure.

5. Route the case to the Card Services dispute queue in the case management system.

metadata.section_path: Card Dispute Procedure > 3. Classification
metadata.title: Card Dispute Procedure

text:
Card Dispute Procedure
3. Classification

Card Services classifies each dispute within one business day of intake. Unauthorized transactions (lost, stolen or counterfeit card; card-not-present fraud) follow the fraud path. Authorized transactions with a merchant problem (goods not received, not as described, duplicate processing, credit not processed) follow the merchant dispute path. Where the member has not first tried to resolve a merchant dispute with the merchant, the analyst documents the reason in the case notes.

metadata.section_path: Card Dispute Procedure > 4. Provisional Credit
metadata.title: Card Dispute Procedure

text:
Card Dispute Procedure
4. Provisional Credit

Provisional credit for the disputed amount is posted within 10 business days of receiving the dispute notice if the investigation has not been completed by then. For accounts opened less than 30 days before the first disputed transaction, provisional credit is posted within 20 business days. The member is notified of the provisional credit, including the amount and date, within two business days of posting.

Provisional credit is not required for credit card disputes, where the disputed amount is instead suspended from the balance and excluded from finance charges while the investigation is open.

metadata.section_path: Card Dispute Procedure > 5. Investigation
metadata.title: Card Dispute Procedure

text:
Card Dispute Procedure
5. Investigation

The investigation must be completed within 45 calendar days of receiving the dispute notice. The period is extended to 90 calendar days for point-of-sale transactions, foreign-initiated transactions, and transactions on accounts opened within the previous 30 days. The analyst reviews authorization data, device and location information, prior dispute history, and any documents supplied by the member or the merchant.

Where a chargeback is appropriate, Card Services submits it to the network no later than 120 calendar days after the transaction settlement date. Supporting documents are attached to the case record, not stored on shared drives.

metadata.section_path: Card Dispute Procedure > 6. Resolution and Member Notification
metadata.title: Card Dispute Procedure

text:
Card Dispute Procedure
6. Resolution and Member Notification

Card Services notifies the member in writing within 3 business days of completing the investigation. If the dispute is resolved in the member's favour, any provisional credit becomes final. If Harbor determines that no error occurred, the notice explains the findings, the member's right to request the documents relied upon, and the date on which provisional credit will be reversed, which must be at least 5 business days after the notice is sent.

metadata.section_path: Card Dispute Procedure > 7. Records Retention
metadata.title: Card Dispute Procedure

text:
Card Dispute Procedure
7. Records Retention

Dispute case records, including Form HCU-DSP-114, correspondence and network submissions, are retained for a minimum of two years from the date of resolution, or longer where litigation or a regulatory examination is pending.

metadata.section_path: Card Dispute Procedure > 8. Escalation
metadata.title: Card Dispute Procedure

text:
Card Dispute Procedure
8. Escalation

Disputes over $5,000, disputes involving a Harbor employee, and any case where the member alleges that Harbor itself made the error are escalated to the Card Services Manager on the day of classification. Complaints about the handling of a dispute are logged in the complaint register in accordance with the Complaint Handling Standard.

metadata.section_path: Debit Card Limits and Controls
metadata.title: Debit Card Limits and Controls

text:
Debit Card Limits and Controls

Member guide | Updated: February 2, 2026 | Applies to: Harbor Visa® debit cards on Retail checking accounts

Your Harbor debit card has daily limits that protect your account if the card is lost, stolen or used without your permission. This guide explains the limits, how to change them, and the controls you can set yourself in the Harbor mobile app — no phone call needed.

metadata.section_path: Debit Card Limits and Controls > Daily Limits
metadata.title: Debit Card Limits and Controls

text:
Debit Card Limits and Controls
Daily Limits

For most members, the standard daily ATM cash withdrawal limit is $500. The card’s daily point-of-sale purchase limit is $3,000, which covers purchases made in stores, online and by phone. Limits reset at midnight Eastern Time. Cash back received at a store counts toward the purchase limit, not the ATM limit.

Premier Checking cardholders may have higher limits based on their relationship with Harbor. Your current limits are shown in the app under Card Controls — Limits.

metadata.section_path: Debit Card Limits and Controls > Requesting a Temporary Increase
metadata.title: Debit Card Limits and Controls

text:
Debit Card Limits and Controls
Requesting a Temporary Increase

If you need to make a large purchase — for example, a car deposit or a café renovation invoice — you can request a temporary increase through the Member Contact Centre or at a branch. Temporary increases last up to 72 hours. We’ll ask you to verify your identity and may ask about the purpose of the transaction. Increases are approved at Harbor’s discretion and are not available on accounts open less than 60 days.

metadata.section_path: Debit Card Limits and Controls > Card Controls in the App
metadata.title: Debit Card Limits and Controls

text:
Debit Card Limits and Controls
Card Controls in the App

- Lock and unlock your card – a locked card declines new purchases and ATM withdrawals, while recurring payments you’ve already set up continue.

- Turn international transactions on or off – transactions outside the United States are declined while this control is off.

- Set spending alerts – receive a notification for any purchase above an amount you choose.

- Block merchant categories – for example, gaming or online marketplaces.

Changes to card controls take effect immediately. Locking your card is not the same as reporting it lost or stolen; if you can’t find your card after checking, report it right away so we can block it and order a replacement.

metadata.section_path: Debit Card Limits and Controls > Travelling
metadata.title: Debit Card Limits and Controls

text:
Debit Card Limits and Controls
Travelling

You don’t need to tell us before you travel, but keeping your phone number and e-mail address up to date helps us reach you if we see unusual activity. Foreign transaction fees are listed in the Schedule of Fees and Charges.

metadata.section_path: Debit Card Limits and Controls > Your Liability
metadata.title: Debit Card Limits and Controls

text:
Debit Card Limits and Controls
Your Liability

Tell us at once if you believe your card has been lost or stolen. Your liability for unauthorized transactions is explained in the Electronic Fund Transfer Agreement and Disclosure you received when you opened your account — a plain-language résumé of the key points is available on request.

metadata.section_path: Loan Late Payment and Collections Policy
metadata.title: Loan Late Payment and Collections Policy

text:
Loan Late Payment and Collections Policy

_Policy number: LN-COL-002 | Version 1.6 | Effective date: May 1, 2026 | Owner: Consumer Lending and Collections_

1. Purpose

This policy describes how Harbor Credit Union treats consumer loan payments that are not received by the due date, the fees that apply, the communications members receive, and the point at which an account is referred for collection. It is intended to balance fair treatment of members experiencing difficulty with the credit union's duty to protect the membership as a whole from loan losses.

metadata.section_path: Loan Late Payment and Collections Policy > 2. Scope
metadata.title: Loan Late Payment and Collections Policy

text:
Loan Late Payment and Collections Policy
2. Scope

This policy applies to closed-end consumer loans, including new and used auto loans, personal loans, and share-secured loans. Credit card accounts, home equity lines of credit and first mortgages are covered by their own agreements and servicing procedures.

metadata.section_path: Loan Late Payment and Collections Policy > 3. Grace Period
metadata.title: Loan Late Payment and Collections Policy

text:
Loan Late Payment and Collections Policy
3. Grace Period

A payment is considered late if it is not received within 15 calendar days after the due date shown on the billing statement. Payments received during the grace period are applied as on-time payments for fee purposes, although interest continues to accrue daily on simple-interest loans until the payment is received.

If the last day of the grace period falls on a weekend or a Federal Reserve holiday, the grace period is extended to the next business day.

metadata.section_path: Loan Late Payment and Collections Policy > 4. Late Fees
metadata.title: Loan Late Payment and Collections Policy

text:
Loan Late Payment and Collections Policy
4. Late Fees

When a payment is late under Section 3, Harbor assesses a single late fee equal to 5% of the scheduled payment amount or $25.00, whichever is less. Only one late fee is charged for any one scheduled payment, and a late fee is never charged because an earlier late fee remains unpaid. Late fees are not charged on loans enrolled in an approved hardship program while the member is meeting the program terms.

metadata.section_path: Loan Late Payment and Collections Policy > 5. Delinquency Communications
metadata.title: Loan Late Payment and Collections Policy

text:
Loan Late Payment and Collections Policy
5. Delinquency Communications

1. Day 5 after the due date: courtesy reminder by e-mail or text alert.

2. Day 16: late notice by mail stating the late fee and the amount now due.

3. Day 30: outbound call from a Collections Specialist to discuss the reason for the delay and repayment options.

4. Day 45: second written notice offering a hardship review appointment.

5. Day 60: notice of right to cure, where required by state law.

metadata.section_path: Loan Late Payment and Collections Policy > 6. Credit Reporting
metadata.title: Loan Late Payment and Collections Policy

text:
Loan Late Payment and Collections Policy
6. Credit Reporting

Harbor reports an account as delinquent to the consumer reporting agencies once a payment is 30 or more days past due. Reporting is accurate and complete, and disputes of credit reporting are investigated within the timeframes required by the Fair Credit Reporting Act.

metadata.section_path: Loan Late Payment and Collections Policy > 7. Collections Referral
metadata.title: Loan Late Payment and Collections Policy

text:
Loan Late Payment and Collections Policy
7. Collections Referral

Accounts that reach 90 days past due are transferred from the Collections Specialist team to the Recovery Unit. The Recovery Unit may recommend repossession of collateral, legal action, or placement with an outside agency, subject to approval by the Collections Manager. All collection activity must comply with applicable consumer protection laws, and members may not be contacted before 8:00 a.m. or after 9:00 p.m. local time.

metadata.section_path: Loan Late Payment and Collections Policy > 8. Hardship Assistance
metadata.title: Loan Late Payment and Collections Policy

text:
Loan Late Payment and Collections Policy
8. Hardship Assistance

Members experiencing temporary hardship may request a payment extension, a skip-a-payment, or a loan modification. A loan may receive no more than two payment extensions in any rolling 12-month period. Hardship requests are reviewed within five business days of receiving the member's completed application and supporting documents.

metadata.section_path: Loan Late Payment and Collections Policy > 9. Charge-Off
metadata.title: Loan Late Payment and Collections Policy

text:
Loan Late Payment and Collections Policy
9. Charge-Off

Consumer loans that remain delinquent are charged off no later than 120 days past due for closed-end loans, unless the Collections Manager documents a reasonable expectation of recovery. Charge-off does not release the member from the obligation to repay.

metadata.section_path: Harbor Credit Union Overdraft Policy
metadata.title: Overdraft Policy

text:
Harbor Credit Union Overdraft Policy

_Policy number: DEP-OD-001 | Version 2.0 | Effective date: March 1, 2024 | Document owner: Deposit Operations | Approved by: Board Risk Committee, January 18, 2024_

metadata.section_path: Harbor Credit Union Overdraft Policy > 1. Purpose and Scope
metadata.title: Overdraft Policy

text:
Harbor Credit Union Overdraft Policy
1. Purpose and Scope

This policy describes how Harbor Credit Union ("Harbor", "we", "us") handles transactions presented against a consumer checking account when the Available Balance is not sufficient to pay them. It applies to all Retail checking products, including Basic Checking, Premier Checking and Student Checking. Business deposit accounts are governed separately by the Business Account Fee Guide and are outside the scope of this policy.

Harbor pays overdrafts at its discretion. Nothing in this policy creates an obligation to pay any item, and Harbor may decline to pay an item even when a member has previously had overdrafts paid.

metadata.section_path: Harbor Credit Union Overdraft Policy > 2. Definitions
metadata.title: Overdraft Policy

text:
Harbor Credit Union Overdraft Policy
2. Definitions

- Available Balance means the ledger balance of the account, less any holds placed on deposits and pending debit card authorizations, plus any pending deposits that have been made available.

- Overdraft means a negative Available Balance created when Harbor pays an item for which funds are not available.

- Courtesy Pay means Harbor's discretionary overdraft service for eligible Retail checking accounts, subject to the limit described in Section 3.

- Overdraft Transfer Protection means an automatic transfer from a linked Primary Share Account (savings) to cover an item that would otherwise overdraw checking.

- Item means any check, ACH debit, recurring debit card payment, bill payment, or other debit presented against the account.

metadata.section_path: Harbor Credit Union Overdraft Policy > 3. Courtesy Pay Eligibility and Limits
metadata.title: Overdraft Policy

text:
Harbor Credit Union Overdraft Policy
3. Courtesy Pay Eligibility and Limits

A checking account is eligible for Courtesy Pay after it has been open for at least 90 days, the primary owner is at least 18 years of age, and deposits totalling at least $250 have posted in each of the two most recent calendar months. Eligible accounts are assigned a Courtesy Pay limit of $500. Harbor may lower or remove the limit if the account is not returned to a positive balance within the timeframe in Section 7.

The Courtesy Pay limit includes the amount of the overdraft and any fees charged. Members may view their current limit in online banking under Account Services.

metadata.section_path: Harbor Credit Union Overdraft Policy > 4. Overdraft Fees
metadata.title: Overdraft Policy

text:
Harbor Credit Union Overdraft Policy
4. Overdraft Fees

Harbor charges an overdraft fee of $32 for each item paid into overdraft, with no more than four (4) such fees assessed per business day. No overdraft fee is charged when the account is overdrawn by $10.00 or less at the end of the business day. Returned item (NSF) fees are listed in the Schedule of Fees and Charges.

Each Overdraft Transfer Protection transfer from a linked Primary Share Account is subject to a $10.00 transfer fee. The transfer fee is assessed for each transfer made.

metadata.section_path: Harbor Credit Union Overdraft Policy > 5. ATM and One-Time Debit Card Transactions
metadata.title: Overdraft Policy

text:
Harbor Credit Union Overdraft Policy
5. ATM and One-Time Debit Card Transactions

Consistent with Regulation E, Harbor will not pay ATM withdrawals or one-time debit card transactions into overdraft under Courtesy Pay unless the member has affirmatively opted in. Members may opt in or revoke their consent at any time at a branch, through the Member Contact Centre, or in online banking. Recurring debit card payments, checks and ACH debits are not affected by this election.

metadata.section_path: Harbor Credit Union Overdraft Policy > 6. Order of Posting
metadata.title: Overdraft Policy

text:
Harbor Credit Union Overdraft Policy
6. Order of Posting

Deposits are credited first. Debit card and ATM transactions are then posted in the order in which they were authorized, followed by checks in check-number order and ACH debits in the order received. Harbor does not re-order transactions to increase the number of overdraft fees.

metadata.section_path: Harbor Credit Union Overdraft Policy > 7. Repayment
metadata.title: Overdraft Policy

text:
Harbor Credit Union Overdraft Policy
7. Repayment

Members are expected to return an overdrawn account to a positive balance promptly. If an account remains overdrawn for 30 consecutive days, Courtesy Pay is suspended. If an account remains overdrawn for 45 consecutive days, it may be closed and the negative balance referred for recovery.

metadata.section_path: Harbor Credit Union Overdraft Policy > 8. Member Notices
metadata.title: Overdraft Policy

text:
Harbor Credit Union Overdraft Policy
8. Member Notices

Harbor sends an overdraft notice by the member's selected delivery method (e-mail, text alert or mail) on the business day after an item is paid into overdraft or returned. Monthly and year-to-date totals of overdraft and returned item fees are shown on each periodic statement.

metadata.section_path: Harbor Credit Union Overdraft Policy > 9. Policy Review
metadata.title: Overdraft Policy

text:
Harbor Credit Union Overdraft Policy
9. Policy Review

This policy is reviewed at least annually by Deposit Operations and Compliance. Version 2.0 supersedes Version 1.3 (effective June 1, 2021). Summary of changes: the Regulation E opt-in section was rewritten, the order of posting was updated to authorization order, and member notice delivery methods were expanded to include text alerts.

metadata.title: Overdraft Policy

text:
Harbor Credit Union Overdraft Policy
1. Purpose and Scope

This policy describes how Harbor Credit Union ("Harbor", "we", "us") handles transactions presented against a consumer checking account when the Available Balance is not sufficient to pay them. It applies to all Retail checking products, including Basic Checking, Premier Checking and Student Checking. Business deposit accounts are governed separately by the Business Account Fee Guide and are outside the scope of this policy.

Harbor pays overdrafts at its discretion. Nothing in this policy creates an obligation to pay any item, and Harbor may decline to pay an item even when a member has previously had overdrafts paid.

metadata.section_path: Privacy Notice
metadata.title: Privacy Notice

text:
Privacy Notice

Rev. 01/2026 — Harbor Credit Union © 2026

Why?

Financial companies choose how they share your personal information. Federal law gives consumers the right to limit some but not all sharing. Federal law also requires us to tell you how we collect, share, and protect your personal information. Please read this notice carefully to understand what we do.

metadata.section_path: Privacy Notice > What?
metadata.title: Privacy Notice

text:
Privacy Notice
What?

The types of personal information we collect and share depend on the product or service you have with us. This information can include your Social Security number and account balances, your transaction history and payment history, and your credit history and credit scores. When you are no longer our member, we continue to share your information as described in this notice.

metadata.section_path: Privacy Notice > How?
metadata.title: Privacy Notice

text:
Privacy Notice
How?

All financial companies need to share members’ personal information to run their everyday business. In the section below, we list the reasons financial companies can share their members’ personal information, the reasons Harbor Credit Union chooses to share, and whether you can limit this sharing.

metadata.section_path: Privacy Notice > Reasons We Can Share Your Personal Information
metadata.title: Privacy Notice

text:
Privacy Notice
Reasons We Can Share Your Personal Information

- For our everyday business purposes — such as to process your transactions, maintain your accounts, respond to court orders and legal investigations, or report to credit bureaus. Does Harbor share? Yes. Can you limit this sharing? No.

- For our marketing purposes — to offer our products and services to you. Does Harbor share? Yes. Can you limit this sharing? No.

- For joint marketing with other financial companies. Does Harbor share? Yes. Can you limit this sharing? No.

- For our affiliates’ everyday business purposes — information about your transactions and experiences. Does Harbor share? No. We don’t share.

- For nonaffiliates to market to you. Does Harbor share? Yes, with the “Harbor Café Rewards” partner program only. Can you limit this sharing? Yes.

metadata.section_path: Privacy Notice > To Limit Our Sharing
metadata.title: Privacy Notice

text:
Privacy Notice
To Limit Our Sharing

Call 1-800-4-HARBOR and choose option 6, visit any branch, or use the “Privacy Choices” page in online banking. Please note: if you are a new member, we can begin sharing your information 30 days from the date we sent this notice. Once we’ve received your request, your opt-out choice takes effect within 30 days and remains in effect until you tell us otherwise. You can contact us at any time to limit our sharing.

How Does Harbor Credit Union Protect My Personal Information?

To protect your personal information from unauthorized access and use, we use security measures that comply with federal law. These measures include computer safeguards, secured files and buildings, and employee training. Our employees are required to complete information security training every year and may access member information only when needed for their job.

How Does Harbor Credit Union Collect My Personal Information?

We collect your personal information, for example, when you open an account or apply for a loan, pay your bills or make deposits, or give us your contact information. We also collect your personal information from others, such as credit bureaus and other companies.

metadata.section_path: Privacy Notice > Definitions
metadata.title: Privacy Notice

text:
Privacy Notice
Definitions

Affiliates are companies related by common ownership or control; Harbor Credit Union has no affiliates. Nonaffiliates are companies not related by common ownership or control; they can be financial and nonfinancial companies, such as our “Harbor Café Rewards” partner. Joint marketing is a formal agreement between nonaffiliated financial companies that together market financial products or services to you; our joint marketing partners include insurance providers.

metadata.section_path: Privacy Notice > Other Important Information
metadata.title: Privacy Notice

text:
Privacy Notice
Other Important Information

Members who reside in states with additional privacy protections will receive a state-specific supplement where required. Harbor Credit Union’s privacy practices are reviewed each year by the Compliance department — the most recent review was completed in December 2025.

metadata.section_path: Fraud Monitoring Thresholds
metadata.title: Fraud Monitoring Thresholds

text:
Fraud Monitoring Thresholds

_Standard ID: RSK-FRD-009 | Version 4.1 | Effective: July 1, 2026 | Owner: Enterprise Fraud Risk | Classification: RESTRICTED. Do not share with members or third parties. Do not quote in member communications._

metadata.section_path: Fraud Monitoring Thresholds > 1. Purpose
metadata.title: Fraud Monitoring Thresholds

text:
Fraud Monitoring Thresholds
1. Purpose

This standard documents the rule thresholds used by the real-time fraud monitoring platform for Retail accounts. Disclosure of these thresholds would allow fraudsters to structure activity to avoid detection. Access is limited to Enterprise Fraud Risk, the Fraud Response Team, Internal Audit and designated Information Security staff.

metadata.section_path: Fraud Monitoring Thresholds > 2. Card Velocity Rules
metadata.title: Fraud Monitoring Thresholds

text:
Fraud Monitoring Thresholds
2. Card Velocity Rules

Velocity Rule VR-3 triggers when a single debit card has more than six (6) card-not-present authorizations within 30 minutes. A VR-3 alert declines further card-not-present authorizations and sends a two-way text alert to the member.

Velocity Rule VR-5 triggers when a card is used at ATMs in two different states within 90 minutes. Velocity Rule VR-7 triggers when three (3) or more declined PIN attempts occur within 24 hours at different terminals.

metadata.section_path: Fraud Monitoring Thresholds > 3. Account Takeover Indicators
metadata.title: Fraud Monitoring Thresholds

text:
Fraud Monitoring Thresholds
3. Account Takeover Indicators

An account takeover score of 720 or above places an online banking session in step-up authentication. A change of phone number or e-mail address followed within 72 hours by an external transfer of more than $2,000 generates a priority alert for manual review.

metadata.section_path: Fraud Monitoring Thresholds > 4. Payment Thresholds
metadata.title: Fraud Monitoring Thresholds

text:
Fraud Monitoring Thresholds
4. Payment Thresholds

Outgoing ACH transfers from Retail accounts above $7,500 in a single business day are held for review when the receiving account was added within the previous 10 days. Person-to-person payments above $800 to a first-time recipient are delayed by four hours. Wire requests are governed by the Wire Transfer Policy; the monitoring platform additionally scores every outgoing wire above $15,000 for account takeover risk.

Card-not-present authorizations from merchants on the internal high-risk merchant list are scored with an additional risk weighting and are declined outright when the account takeover score is 650 or above. First-use international card-present transactions in countries on the elevated-risk list generate a text alert but are not declined unless another rule also triggers.

metadata.section_path: Fraud Monitoring Thresholds > 5. Tuning and Review
metadata.title: Fraud Monitoring Thresholds

text:
Fraud Monitoring Thresholds
5. Tuning and Review

Thresholds are reviewed monthly by the Fraud Rules Committee using false-positive rates, confirmed fraud losses and member friction metrics. Changes are documented in the rules change log and approved by the Chief Risk Officer. Emergency changes may be made by the Fraud Response Team lead and must be ratified at the next committee meeting.

metadata.section_path: Fraud Monitoring Thresholds > 6. Handling
metadata.title: Fraud Monitoring Thresholds

text:
Fraud Monitoring Thresholds
6. Handling

This document must not be stored in member-facing knowledge bases, attached to e-mails sent outside Harbor, or quoted in scripts. Contact centre agents who receive questions about why a transaction was declined should use the approved response in the Declined Transaction Script without referencing any threshold.

metadata.section_path: Savings Account Terms and Conditions
metadata.title: Savings Account Terms and Conditions

text:
Savings Account Terms and Conditions

Form DEP-TC-003 | Revised January 1, 2026

1. Membership and Par Value

To become a member of Harbor Credit Union you must meet the field of membership requirements in our bylaws and purchase and maintain the par value of one share in a Primary Share Account. The par value of a share is $5.00. If the balance of your Primary Share Account falls below the par value, your membership may be terminated after written notice.

metadata.section_path: Savings Account Terms and Conditions > 2. Dividends
metadata.title: Savings Account Terms and Conditions

text:
Savings Account Terms and Conditions
2. Dividends

Dividends are paid from current income and available earnings after required transfers to reserves. The dividend rate and Annual Percentage Yield on savings accounts are variable and may change at any time as determined by the Board of Directors. Dividends are compounded daily and credited monthly for the Primary Share Account, Youth Savings and Money Market accounts.

You must maintain a minimum daily balance of $100 in your Primary Share Account to earn dividends. If the daily balance is below this amount on any day, no dividends are earned for that day. Harbor uses the daily balance method, which applies a daily periodic rate to the principal in the account each day.

metadata.section_path: Savings Account Terms and Conditions > 3. Dividend Period
metadata.title: Savings Account Terms and Conditions

text:
Savings Account Terms and Conditions
3. Dividend Period

The Dividend Period is monthly. For example, the beginning date of the first dividend period of the calendar year is January 1 and the ending date is January 31. All other dividend periods follow the same pattern. If you close your account before dividends are credited, you will receive the accrued dividends through the date of closure.

metadata.section_path: Savings Account Terms and Conditions > 4. Transaction Limitations
metadata.title: Savings Account Terms and Conditions

text:
Savings Account Terms and Conditions
4. Transaction Limitations

You may make an unlimited number of deposits. Harbor limits withdrawals and transfers out of each savings account to six (6) per calendar month by preauthorized, automatic, telephone or online transfer. Transactions in excess of this limit are subject to the excessive withdrawal fee shown below and repeated excess activity may result in the account being converted to a checking account.

metadata.section_path: Savings Account Terms and Conditions > 5. Fees Applicable to Savings
metadata.title: Savings Account Terms and Conditions

text:
Savings Account Terms and Conditions
5. Fees Applicable to Savings

Fee | Amount
Excessive withdrawal (after six per month) | $10.00 each
Account closed within 90 days of opening | $25.00
Returned deposited item | $15.00 per item
Money Market balance below $2,500 minimum | $8.00 per month

metadata.section_path: Savings Account Terms and Conditions > 6. Dormant Accounts and Unclaimed Property
metadata.title: Savings Account Terms and Conditions

text:
Savings Account Terms and Conditions
6. Dormant Accounts and Unclaimed Property

An account with no member-initiated activity for twelve months is classified as dormant. Dormant account fees are listed in the Schedule of Fees and Charges. If an account remains inactive for the period set by state law, Harbor is required to transfer the funds to the state as unclaimed property.

metadata.section_path: Savings Account Terms and Conditions > 7. Deposits and Holds
metadata.title: Savings Account Terms and Conditions

text:
Savings Account Terms and Conditions
7. Deposits and Holds

Funds deposited to savings are available according to the Funds Availability Policy. Harbor may refuse any deposit, limit the amount that may be deposited, or return all or part of a deposit.

metadata.section_path: Savings Account Terms and Conditions > 8. Governing Law
metadata.title: Savings Account Terms and Conditions

text:
Savings Account Terms and Conditions
8. Governing Law

These terms are governed by the bylaws of Harbor Credit Union, federal law and regulations, and the laws of the state in which the credit union is chartered. If any provision is found unenforceable, the remaining provisions remain in effect.

metadata.section_path: Share Certificate Account Disclosure
metadata.title: Share Certificate Account Disclosure

text:
Share Certificate Account Disclosure

_Disclosure form DEP-DSC-017 | Effective: July 1, 2026 | This disclosure supplements the Savings Account Terms and Conditions._

Rate Information

The dividend rate and Annual Percentage Yield (APY) for your Share Certificate are set on the date the certificate is opened and are fixed for the term. Current rates are published on the Deposit Rate Sheet and are available at any branch. The APY assumes dividends remain on deposit until maturity; a withdrawal of dividends will reduce earnings.

metadata.section_path: Share Certificate Account Disclosure > Compounding and Crediting
metadata.title: Share Certificate Account Disclosure

text:
Share Certificate Account Disclosure
Compounding and Crediting

Dividends are compounded daily and credited monthly. You may elect to have dividends credited to the certificate, transferred to your Primary Share Account, or transferred to a Harbor checking account. The dividend period is monthly, beginning on the first calendar day of the month and ending on the last calendar day of the month.

metadata.section_path: Share Certificate Account Disclosure > Minimum Balance Requirements
metadata.title: Share Certificate Account Disclosure

text:
Share Certificate Account Disclosure
Minimum Balance Requirements

The minimum deposit to open a Share Certificate is $1,000. You must maintain a balance of at least $1,000 in the certificate for the full term to obtain the disclosed APY. Balance tiers are determined by the opening deposit.

metadata.section_path: Share Certificate Account Disclosure > Transaction Limitations
metadata.title: Share Certificate Account Disclosure

text:
Share Certificate Account Disclosure
Transaction Limitations

After the certificate is opened, you may not make additional deposits until maturity. Withdrawals of principal before maturity are permitted only as a full withdrawal and are subject to the early withdrawal penalty described below.

metadata.section_path: Share Certificate Account Disclosure > Early Withdrawal Penalty
metadata.title: Share Certificate Account Disclosure

text:
Share Certificate Account Disclosure
Early Withdrawal Penalty

If you withdraw principal before the maturity date, a penalty equal to 90 days of dividends applies to certificates with terms of 12 months or less. For certificates with terms longer than 12 months, a penalty equal to 180 days of dividends applies. The penalty is calculated on the amount withdrawn at the dividend rate in effect on the certificate, and it may reduce principal if dividends earned are less than the penalty.

The penalty is waived when a withdrawal is made because an owner has died or has been declared legally incompetent by a court.

metadata.section_path: Share Certificate Account Disclosure > Renewal and Grace Period
metadata.title: Share Certificate Account Disclosure

text:
Share Certificate Account Disclosure
Renewal and Grace Period

Certificates renew automatically at maturity for the same term at the rate then in effect. You have a grace period of 10 calendar days after maturity to withdraw funds or change the term without penalty. We will send you a maturity notice at least 30 days before a certificate of more than 12 months matures.

metadata.section_path: Share Certificate Account Disclosure > Adding Owners and Beneficiaries
metadata.title: Share Certificate Account Disclosure

text:
Share Certificate Account Disclosure
Adding Owners and Beneficiaries

You may add a joint owner or name payable-on-death beneficiaries when the certificate is opened or at renewal. Changes to ownership during the term may require the certificate to be closed and reopened, which would be treated as an early withdrawal. Individual Retirement Account (IRA) certificates are subject to additional terms in the IRA disclosure.

metadata.section_path: Share Certificate Account Disclosure > Insurance
metadata.title: Share Certificate Account Disclosure

text:
Share Certificate Account Disclosure
Insurance

Member accounts are federally insured by the National Credit Union Administration up to at least $250,000 per member, per ownership category.

Wire Transfer Policy
Policy number: PAY-WT-004 | Revision 2026-02 | Effective date: February 16, 2026 | Owner: Payments
Operations | Applies to: Retail accounts
1. Purpose
This policy establishes the requirements Harbor Credit Union follows when sending and receiving
funds transfers by wire on behalf of Retail members. Wire transfers are generally final once sent
and are a frequent target of fraud, so the controls in this policy are designed to confirm that every
outgoing wire is authorized by the member, is accurate, and complies with applicable law,
including Article 4A of the Uniform Commercial Code, the Bank Secrecy Act, and sanctions
screening requirements.
2. Scope
This policy applies to domestic and international wire transfers initiated from or received into
Retail share and checking accounts. Business accounts are subject to the Business Account Fee
Guide and the Business Services Agreement. Automated Clearing House (ACH) transfers,
person-to-person payments, and internal transfers between Harbor accounts are not wire transfers
and are outside the scope of this policy.
3. Definitions
• Business day means Monday through Friday, excluding Federal Reserve holidays.
• Domestic

wire means a funds transfer to a beneficiary account at a financial institution located
in the United States.
• International wire means a funds transfer to a beneficiary account at a financial institution
located outside the United States, in US dollars or a foreign currency.
• Callback verification means a telephone call placed by Harbor staff to a phone number already
on file for the member, not a number supplied in the wire request.
4. Authorized Channels
Members may request an outgoing wire in person at any Harbor branch or through online banking
once the member has enrolled in online wire service. The Member Contact Centre may answer
questions about a wire but does not accept wire instructions by telephone, e-mail or text message.
Instructions received by e-mail must be treated as a potential fraud attempt and reported to the
Fraud Response Team.
Online wire service is available to members whose account has been open for at least 90 days and
who have completed enhanced authentication enrollment. The online daily limit for outgoing wires

is $50,000 per member. Requests above this limit must be completed in branch with valid
government-issued photo identification.
5. Processing Cutoff Times
Domestic wire requests received and verified by 3:00 p.m. Eastern Time on a business day are
processed the same business day. Requests received after the cutoff, or on a day that is not a
business day, are processed on the next business day. International wire requests must be received
and verified by 1:00 p.m. Eastern Time to be released the same business day; delivery to the
beneficiary may take one to five business days depending on the destination country and
intermediary banks.
6. Fees
The fee for an outgoing domestic wire from a Retail account is $25.00 per wire. Outgoing
international wires from Retail accounts are charged $45.00 per wire, plus any intermediary or
beneficiary bank charges deducted from the transferred amount. Incoming wires credited to a
Retail account are charged $15.00 per wire. Fees are debited from the funding account at the time
the wire is sent or received and are not refunded if a wire is returned by the receiving institution.
7. Verification and Fraud Controls
Any online wire request above $25,000

requires a callback verification before release. Branch wire
requests require the member to sign the wire request form in the presence of staff after the details
have been read back. Every outgoing wire is screened against the Office of Foreign Assets Control
(OFAC) sanctions lists before release; a potential match places the wire on hold until Compliance
clears or rejects it.
Staff must place a wire on hold and escalate to the Fraud Response Team if the member appears to
be acting under instruction from a third party, if the request follows a recent change to the
member's contact details, or if the beneficiary details were supplied in an e-mail claiming to be
from a title company, employer or government agency.
8. Errors, Recalls and Returns
A member who believes a wire was sent in error must notify Harbor as soon as possible. Harbor
will request a recall from the receiving institution but cannot guarantee the return of funds once a
wire has been released. Returned funds are credited to the member's account net of any charges
imposed by the receiving or intermediary institutions.
9. Recordkeeping

Wire request forms, callback records, OFAC screening results and confirmation messages are
retained for five years from the date of the transfer. Records must be retrievable by the member's
account number and by the wire reference number.
10. Exceptions
Exceptions to this policy, including fee waivers above $100 in a calendar year for a single member,
require written approval from the Payments Operations Manager. Exceptions to the verification
requirements in Section 7 are not permitted.

metadata.section_path: Frequently Asked Questions
metadata.title: Frequently Asked Questions

text:
Frequently Asked Questions

Find quick answers to the questions members ask us most. Can't find what you need? Contact us and we'll be happy to help.

How do I become a member of Harbor Credit Union?

Anyone who lives, works, worships or attends school in our service area, and their immediate family members, can join. A minimum deposit of $5.00 in a Primary Share Account establishes your membership. You can open your membership online in about ten minutes or at any branch.

metadata.section_path: Frequently Asked Questions > What are the Member Contact Centre hours?
metadata.title: Frequently Asked Questions

text:
Frequently Asked Questions
What are the Member Contact Centre hours?

Our Member Contact Centre is available Monday through Friday from 7:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. and Saturday from 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. Eastern Time. You can reach us at 1-800-4-HARBOR. To report a lost or stolen card outside these hours, choose option 1 at any time and your call will be routed to our 24-hour card service.

metadata.section_path: Frequently Asked Questions > How do I order checks?
metadata.title: Frequently Asked Questions

text:
Frequently Asked Questions
How do I order checks?

You can reorder checks in online banking under Account Services, or call the Member Contact Centre. Your first box of Harbor standard checks is free with Premier Checking.

When will my direct deposit be available?

Payroll and government direct deposits are made available as soon as Harbor receives the payment file, which may be up to two days before the scheduled payment date. Early availability depends on when the payer sends the file and is not guaranteed.

metadata.section_path: Frequently Asked Questions > How do I set up e-statements?
metadata.title: Frequently Asked Questions

text:
Frequently Asked Questions
How do I set up e-statements?

Sign in to online banking, open the Documents tab, and select Go Paperless. You will receive an e-mail each month when your statement is ready. Members who receive e-statements are not charged the paper statement fee.

metadata.section_path: Frequently Asked Questions > What should I do if I see a charge I don't recognize?
metadata.title: Frequently Asked Questions

text:
Frequently Asked Questions
What should I do if I see a charge I don't recognize?

First check with anyone else who uses the card, and look for a merchant name that may differ from the store name. If you still don't recognize the charge, contact us right away so we can review it and, if needed, start a dispute on your behalf.

metadata.section_path: Frequently Asked Questions > Can I get my account and routing numbers online?
metadata.title: Frequently Asked Questions

text:
Frequently Asked Questions
Can I get my account and routing numbers online?

Yes. In online banking or the mobile app, select the account and choose Account Details. For your security, the full account number is shown only after you confirm a one-time passcode.

metadata.section_path: Frequently Asked Questions > Do you charge a fee to close an account?
metadata.title: Frequently Asked Questions

text:
Frequently Asked Questions
Do you charge a fee to close an account?

There is no fee to close an account unless it is closed within 90 days of opening. Please see our Schedule of Fees and Charges for details.

How do I update my address or phone number?

You can update your mailing address, e-mail and phone number in online banking under Profile. Changes to your phone number trigger a verification code to the new number and a notice to your previous e-mail address.

metadata.section_path: Frequently Asked Questions > Is my money insured?
metadata.title: Frequently Asked Questions

text:
Frequently Asked Questions
Is my money insured?

Yes. Deposits at Harbor are federally insured by the National Credit Union Administration up to at least $250,000 per member, per ownership category.

Can I make a loan payment from another financial institution?

Yes. You can make a one-time or recurring payment from an external account in online banking under Transfers, or mail a check to our loan payment address shown on your statement.

metadata.section_path: Frequently Asked Questions > How do I apply for a loan?
metadata.title: Frequently Asked Questions

text:
Frequently Asked Questions
How do I apply for a loan?

Apply in the mobile app, in online banking, by phone, or at any branch. Most applications receive a decision within one business day. Auto loan rates are shown on our Auto Loan Product Comparison sheet.

metadata.section_path: Mobile and Online Banking Help
metadata.title: Mobile and Online Banking Help

text:
Mobile and Online Banking Help

Use this page to get started with Harbor online banking and the Harbor mobile app, and to troubleshoot common issues.

Signing In

I forgot my password. What should I do?

Select Forgot Password on the sign-in screen. We will send a one-time passcode to the phone number or e-mail address on file. Your new password must be at least 12 characters and cannot match any of your last five passwords.

Why is my access locked?

After five (5) consecutive failed sign-in attempts your access is locked for 30 minutes. After the lockout period you can try again, or reset your password immediately using Forgot Password. If you did not attempt to sign in, contact us, because someone else may be trying to access your account.

Can I use fingerprint or face recognition?

Yes. After you sign in with your password once on a device, go to Settings and turn on biometric sign-in. Biometric sign-in is tied to the device, so you will need to enable it again on a new phone.

metadata.section_path: Mobile and Online Banking Help > Mobile Check Deposit
metadata.title: Mobile and Online Banking Help

text:
Mobile and Online Banking Help
Mobile Check Deposit

Question | Answer

How much can I deposit? | The standard daily limit for mobile check deposit is $5,000 per member, with a rolling 30-day limit of $15,000. Members with accounts open less than 90 days have a daily limit of $1,500.
When will funds be available? | Deposits received before 6:00 p.m. Eastern Time on a business day are generally available the next business day. Some deposits may be held longer; we will notify you if a hold is placed.
What should I write on the check? | Endorse the back with your signature and the words "For mobile deposit at Harbor CU only". Keep the paper check for 30 days, then destroy it.

metadata.section_path: Mobile and Online Banking Help > Paying People and Bills
metadata.title: Mobile and Online Banking Help

text:
Mobile and Online Banking Help
Paying People and Bills

How much can I send with Harbor Pay?

Harbor Pay person-to-person payments are limited to $1,000 per day and $3,000 per rolling 30 days. Payments to a recipient you have paid before usually arrive within minutes.

When will my bill payment arrive?

Electronic bill payments are delivered within two business days. Payees that cannot accept electronic payments receive a paper check, which can take up to five business days. Schedule payments at least five business days before the due date to be safe.

metadata.section_path: Mobile and Online Banking Help > Alerts and Security
metadata.title: Mobile and Online Banking Help

text:
Mobile and Online Banking Help
Alerts and Security

Turn on balance, deposit and transaction alerts in Settings under Alerts. Harbor will never ask you for your password, full card number or one-time passcode by phone, e-mail or text. If you receive a request like this, do not respond and contact us using the number on the back of your card.

metadata.section_path: Mobile and Online Banking Help > Supported Devices and Browsers
metadata.title: Mobile and Online Banking Help

text:
Mobile and Online Banking Help
Supported Devices and Browsers

The Harbor mobile app supports the two most recent major versions of iOS and Android. Online banking supports the current and previous versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari. Older browsers may display pages incorrectly or be blocked for security reasons.
